key_insight: For bounded-degree max-LINSAT over finite fields, the best possible improvement over random guessing scales only as O(1/sqrt(D)), and DQI can match this scaling only with quantum, not classical, decoding.
engineering_relevance: This sets the benchmark for bounded-degree quantum optimization pipelines: any practical speedup must come from constants, decoder design, and problem structure rather than asymptotic scaling.
method: Prove NP-hardness of exceeding r/q + O_{q,r}(1/sqrt(D)) for max-Ek-LINSAT(q,r) with bounded degree D.
Extend the bounded-degree approximation barrier from Boolean XORSAT to arbitrary finite fields F_q.
Analyze decoded quantum interferometry on (k,D)-regular instances and compare classical vs quantum decoders.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a complexity-theoretic hardness result matched to known bounded-degree algorithmic scaling, plus an information-theoretic 1/sqrt(D log D) limitation for classical decoders in DQI.
watch_item: The results constrain asymptotic approximation guarantees, but they do not by themselves imply a practical advantage for real hardware or finite-size instances.
paper_title: Approximability limits for bounded-degree max-LINSAT and implications for decoded quantum interferometry
